newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia trade deficit cut in first 8 months.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia trade deficit cut in first 8 months.

text.p: Tunisia's trade deficit during the first eight months of 1996 stood at 1.432 billion dinars, down from 1.577 billion dinars during the same period last year, official figures showed.
Exports amounted 3.472 billion dinars, up by 2.8 percent compared to 3.378 billion dinars, and imports were worth 4.905 billion dinars, down by one percent from 4.956 billion dinars.

The figures, obtained by Reuters and not yet officially released, showed the decrease in imports was partly due to a drop in food purchasings by 30.3 percent, after they increased by 80.7 percent during the same period last year because of drought.
Food imports amounted 213 million dinars during the eights months of 1996 from 344 million dinars during the same period in 1995.

Consumption goods exports amounted to 1.873 billion dinars, up by 5.8 percent from 1.770 billion dinars, and imports were worth 1.697 billion dinars up by 6.4 percent compared to 1.595 billion dinars.

Energy exports amounted to 316 million dinars, up by 6.4 percent compared to 297 million dinars, and imports were worth 368 million dinars, up by 16.7 percent compared to 315 million dinars. ($=0.97 dinar)
